justifications.functional_suitability: Scoring Engine (Rule Evaluator, Model Runner) and Case Management (Case Workflow Engine) cover R-01 and R-02. R-03 zero-downtime rule/model updates is only implied by signed artifacts in Model Runner; no update mechanism or rule management component exists. Review routing to Case Management is undefined.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Lambda Provisioned Concurrency in Go, in-memory Rule Evaluator, Feature Store (ElastiCache <5ms), and asynchronous Audit Logger with SQS match the 50ms P99 target. Gaps: the extra Edge Tokenizer Lambda hop, no load-sizing evidence for 3,000 TPS, and an inconsistent Fargate/Lambda description.
justifications.compatibility: Merchant gateway integration via API Gateway, gRPC/mTLS, and OIDC/SAML IdP are named. However, protocols are inconsistent (gRPC at L1 versus HTTPS at the API Gateway), and the IdP lacks container-level relationships, so interoperability details remain partly unspecified.
justifications.usability: Analyst SPA with a Case Workflow Engine prioritization queue serves analysts, and the Compliance & Risk Officer gets S3 Object Lock access. But officers only get raw SDK access with no UI, and no explanation view exists for decisions.
justifications.reliability: SQS FIFO with Dead-Letter Queue and serverless managed services give some resilience. But there is no fail-open fallback for R-07, no multi-AZ or recovery design, no timeouts or circuit breakers, and Scoring Engine failure would block payments.
justifications.security: Edge Tokenizer Lambda, AWS WAF, KMS, PAN stripping in API Handler, mTLS, MFA OIDC, VPC Interface Endpoint, signed model artifacts, and S3 Object Lock compliance mode address R-05/R-06. Gaps: no explicit RBAC masking for analysts and no detailed PCI segmentation.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container decomposition (API Gateway, Scoring Engine, Case Management, Data Layer) with decoupled audit queue. However, the Infrastructure Services pseudo-component, overlapping S3/SQS responsibilities across containers, and inconsistent models hurt clarity for a three-person team.
justifications.portability: The design is tightly bound to AWS services (Lambda, Aurora, SQS, Firehose, KMS) with no abstraction layers. It does fit the AWS eu-west-1 target, but replaceability is not addressed and no infrastructure-as-code is mentioned.

sensitivity_points: Two Lambda hops plus API Gateway inside 50 ms budget
Provisioned concurrency sizing for 3,000 TPS
Redis feature read latency
tradeoffs: Serverless elasticity versus tail latency and fixed budget
Edge tokenization adds latency but improves PCI scope
PERF-01.justification: In-memory rules, ONNX models, Redis features and provisioned concurrency are sound. But API Gateway, tokenizer Lambda and scoring Lambda chain plus gRPC/HTTP inconsistency threaten P99 50 ms; no capacity or cost evidence.

sensitivity_points: Shared Redis or Aurora contention
Aurora ACU scaling during peak
tradeoffs: Separate stores isolate load but increase cost
PERF-02.justification: Case management is separate (Fargate, Aurora, CloudFront SPA) from the Lambda scoring path, so analyst load barely touches scoring. Scoring uses Redis, not Aurora. Case screens under 2 s are plausible; no explicit caching or load test.

sensitivity_points: No fallback decision path defined
Single scoring path, no timeout/default policy
tradeoffs: Fail-open reduces blocking but raises fraud risk
AVAIL-01.justification: No fallback scorer, circuit breaker, timeout default or fail-open policy exists. Lambda gives some resilience but nothing ensures decisions within 1 minute, and no fallback decisions are audited. Observability only detects.

sensitivity_points: SQS availability and send failure handling in Lambda
Lambda lacks local buffer; in-memory Go channels lost on crash
FIFO throughput limit at 3,000 TPS
tradeoffs: Async decoupling protects latency but risks loss
AVAIL-02.justification: SQS decouples audit from decisions, with DLQ and Firehose to S3. But the audit logger uses in-memory channel batching in Lambda, risking loss on crash, and there is no behaviour if SQS fails. FIFO limits are a concern.

sensitivity_points: No model registry, versioning or traffic shifting described
Model version recorded in audit payload not explicit
tradeoffs: Signed artifact verification adds startup time but gives integrity
MOD-01.justification: Signed model artifacts loaded from S3 and Lambda versions/aliases could support zero-downtime swaps. But there is no explicit deployment, canary, rollback mechanism or model version in decisions; requires significant additions.

sensitivity_points: Rules are in-memory bytecode with no authoring or distribution path
Rule IDs not recorded in decisions
tradeoffs: In-memory evaluation is fast but harder to update dynamically
MOD-02.justification: Rule Evaluator runs in-memory bytecode, but no rule management, hot reload, authoring, approval or distribution mechanism exists. Audit payload does not state rules applied. Analysts have no rule-editing interface.

sensitivity_points: Tokenization at edge keeps PAN away from analysts
Anomalous analyst access detection not defined
Data Layer contents of PAN unspecified
tradeoffs: MFA and RBAC add friction but limit compromise
SEC-01.justification: Edge tokenization, PAN stripping, MFA and RBAC mean analysts likely never see PANs. But no analyst access anomaly detection or 15-minute alerting is specified; CloudWatch/SNS are generic. Detection is a gap.

sensitivity_points: Payload content: inputs, model version, explanation not specified
No query/retrieval index over S3 archive
Object Lock compliance mode
tradeoffs: WORM storage ensures tamper evidence but hinders retrieval
SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock compliance mode with 7-year retention gives tamper-evident storage. But explanation content, model/rule versions and inputs are not specified in records, and there is no retrieval or query tooling (e.g. Athena), so one-day reproduction is uncertain.

elements: Case Workflow Engine with Prioritization Queue
